brief: The canvas displays a complex, multi-stranded knot structure, appearing woven and tightly bound. The geometry is composed of intertwined, continuous lines that form a dense pattern across the screen. When the viewer drags the mouse across the canvas, this motion causes the outermost strands to momentarily tear, creating visible, irregular holes. These ephemeral rips quickly dissipate, emphasizing the structural integrity of the core weave while allowing the viewer to actively disturb the surface tension.

statement: This sketch creates a complex, multi-stranded knot structure using WebGL rendering to achieve dense weaving patterns across the screen. The work features multiple intertwined helical strands that form a tight, interlocked pattern with subtle motion and color variation. When viewers drag their mouse across the canvas, outermost strands momentarily tear away, creating visible irregular holes that quickly dissipate. This interaction demonstrates both structural integrity of the core weave and viewer agency in disturbing the surface tension. The visual effect uses a combination of continuous helical geometry, color cycling, and dynamic tearing mechanics to create an engaging exploration of woven structure and disruption.
